intro: KMZ to GPX turns Google Earth or Google My Maps KMZ files into GPX for your GPS, watch or route app. A KMZ is a KML compressed into a ZIP together with its icons and images; here we open it, read its main document (doc.kml) and convert its points, routes and tracks.

Places become waypoints with their name and description, and lines become tracks, including those inside folders or a MultiGeometry. If the KMZ carries gx:Track tracks with each point's time, those times are kept in the GPX.

Whatever GPX cannot hold is left out: polygons (we tell you how many), styles, icons and the images in the ZIP. The ZIP is checked before it is opened, so a crafted file cannot tie up the server by decompressing endlessly.

The KMZ is converted on our server. XML files (GPX and KML) are read without loading DTDs or external entities, out-of-range coordinates are discarded and there is a limit of 2 million points and 50 MB per file. You can convert up to 20 files at once and download them in a ZIP.

faq.q: What is the difference between KML and KMZ?
faq.a: A KMZ is a compressed KML that may carry its icons and photos inside. For GPX only the KML matters; if you have the .kml on its own, use KML to GPX.

faq.q: What if the KMZ holds several KML files?
faq.a: We use doc.kml, which is the main one; if there is none, the KML in the shallowest folder.

faq.q: Can I turn the GPX into another format afterwards?
faq.a: Yes: GPX to GeoJSON for web maps or GPX to KML to go back to Google Earth.
